release: MAJOR: each tab is now true to its name, and that changes what a Site Audit score covers. Content findings move to Content & SEO — mojibake and unresolved tokens (FUNC-008) and misspellings (FUNC-009) were only ever technical-tab findings because that is where the advisory pass happened to fold them. They now run on the content tab and no longer on Site Audit. THE COST, STATED PLAINLY: in the Copy Review suite these rows are advisory, so those two rules are flagged but no longer scored anywhere, and a Site Audit score from 5.x is NOT comparable to one from 6.x because its denominator no longer contains them. That is what the major version records. Fixing this surfaced two defects that would have shipped silently. First, the advisory pass pushed content rows into the FUNCTIONAL suite behind a guard, and a Content & SEO run has no functional suite because it skips every suite except SEO — so the rows were built and silently dropped, and simply enabling the passes there would have delivered nothing at all. They now fall back to the Copy Review suite. Second, and caught only by checking rather than by the test suite: the Copy Review pass was guarded on the copy suite not already existing, which was correct only while nothing else could create it. The content passes now can, and they run first, so the guard saw a suite that existed and skipped the entire Copy Review scan — measured, a Content and SEO run emitted the two content rows and ZERO of COPY-001 through COPY-006. Presence of a suite is not evidence that the pass which owns it ever ran. Both orderings are now asserted so no caller has to know the pass order.
